definition: The number of babies who die in their first 28 days of life, per 1,000 live births.
District Health Information Software 2: the open-source system Tanzania uses to collect and report routine health data from hospitals.
NEST360 Neonatal Inpatient Database: a detailed, patient-level record of newborn care used here as a cross-check.
Regional Referral Hospital: a secondary-level hospital serving a region; there are 28 in this study.
A zonal or national hospital offering the most advanced care and teaching; there are 7 in this study.
Whether a hospital actually filed its reports: here, the share of months a facility reported newborn deaths.
Whether a hospital's numbers stay stable and believable year to year, within WHO's plus-or-minus 33% band.
Whether routine numbers match trusted outside sources like national surveys or UN estimates.
The UN Sustainable Development Goal target to cut newborn deaths to under 12 per 1,000 live births by 2030.
UN Inter-agency Group for Child Mortality Estimation: produces internationally comparable child-death estimates.
Demographic and Health Survey: a large national household survey used to estimate death rates.
A baby born showing signs of life, used as the denominator for the death rate.
Births that happen outside a health facility: about 20% in Tanzania, whose outcomes routine facility data can miss.
